Huber delta 0.5 achieved validation MSE close to baseline, with its best checkpoint at epoch 62. Delta was applied to the standardized target.

Reference model: validation MSE 358.80 kg².
Baseline neural network achieved validation MSE of 320.41 kg² and serves as the reference for Part B.
Batch size 16 achieved the best validation MSE among batch-size experiments (320.11 kg²), slightly outperforming the baseline. It reached its best checkpoint early at epoch 22.
Batch size 32 produced almost identical validation performance to the baseline, with a best MSE of 320.42 kg². It converged to its best checkpoint at epoch 22.
Batch size 128 achieved validation MSE slightly better than the baseline. However, its best checkpoint occurred late at epoch 90, indicating slower convergence.

Batch size 256 produced worse validation performance than the baseline. Its best checkpoint occurred at epoch 95, suggesting that larger batches required more training to reach their best performance.
Batch size 512 resulted in higher validation MSE than smaller batch sizes and did not trigger early stopping before reaching the 100-epoch limit.
Batch size 1024 further increased validation MSE. The model continued training until the maximum epoch limit without triggering early stopping.
Batch size 2048 achieved the worst validation MSE among batch-size experiments. The result suggests that excessively large batches reduced optimization effectiveness under the fixed training budget.
